d.d: A visual representation of an area, whether real or imaginary, showing the relative positions of places and other features.
d.x: a map of Australia, a map of Lilliput

d.d: A graphical or logical representation of any structure or system, showing the positions of or relationships between its components.
d.x: a map of the Earth's magnetic field

d.d: A function, especially a function satisfying a certain property (e.g. continuity, linearity, etc.; see Usage notes).
To represent by means of a map.
d.x: This large atlas maps the whole world in very great detail.

d.d: To create a map of; to examine or survey in order to gather information for a map.
d.x: The team is mapping the route of the new railway line.

d.d: To have a direct relationship; to correspond.
d.x: This doesn't map to my understanding of how things should work.

d.d: Any member of any species of genus Acer, characterized by (usually) palmate, five-lobed leaves and winged seeds, and often grown for syrup or wood

A small tree (Acer campestre), known as the common maple, field maple, or hedge maple, which has palmate leaves with five lobes and winged seeds, and is chiefly native to East Asia, Europe, North Africa, and North America.

Often preceded by a descriptive word: a tree of the genus Acer; especially the sugar maple (Acer saccharum) native to North America which has brightly colored autumn foliage and is the primary source of maple syrup.
Of the light-brown colour of the wood of a maple tree (etymology 1, noun sense 3).
Of the flavour of, or made with, maple syrup.
plural of maple
Acronym of methylacetylene propadiene propane.
